text: A few mobile food vendors in Toronto use clean, silent, inexpensive grid electricity to power their operations. However, most mobile food vendors in Toronto rely on noisy, polluting, gas or diesel generators to provide the power they need. In areas crowded with mobile food vendors, the cumulative effect of these fossil fuel generators can cause noticeable air pollution, and enough noise to disturb those living or working nearby. The cost of the generator and the fuel can also be a material financial burden for the food vendors. The city of New York has launched a pilot project in Flushing Meadows-Corona Park that allows mobile food cart vendors to inexpensively rent clean, rechargeable batteries instead, according to the Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice .
